name: Antelope
label: Dischord
lede: Antelope had one guitar, three players and no fixed drummer: Bee Elvy and Mike Andre swapped kit and bass, and Justin Moyer played guitar over both. Dischord put out three records in five years, then the band quit in 2008.

eras.title: Two Vertebrates and a Guapo
eras.text: Bee Elvy and Mike Andre had played in The Vertebrates; Justin Moyer came from El Guapo. Put together in Washington in 2001, they made one guitar and two rotating rhythm sections the whole plan.

years.p: Dischord credits [[Justin Moyer|68cb15fd-5c0c-4b60-ad06-935ac0756a4d]] with guitar and vocals, and [[Bee Elvy|05615fd4-be3f-489f-aa7c-cc3d14e4c4e9]] and [[Mike Andre|18f336ed-8cdb-4b22-9186-daedae20bf66]] each with drums, bass and vocals. Elvy and Andre traded instruments as the songs needed.
years.xp:
Elvy and Andre came out of The Vertebrates. Moyer was still in [[El Guapo|be23bf0a-67c6-4b2f-ba2a-89d983f5ebdd]], which had landed on Dischord with super/system in 2001. According to Wikipedia, he was diagnosed with epilepsy that year, which put his duo project Edie Sedgwick on hold.

Antelope gave Moyer a different outlet: minimal, repetitive, built on gaps as much as notes.

eras.title: On the road with Q and Not U and Black Eyes
eras.text: The first record was a co-release with Bug Records. Then came a September 2003 US tour with Q and Not U and Black Eyes, and by 2004 Ian MacKaye was producing the band at Inner Ear.

years.h: Six songs with Phil Manley of Trans Am
years.p: Antelope recorded the EP with Manley of [[Trans Am|7c5acaaa-3f74-4e16-82b2-f8046fce4338]] at National Recording Studios in March 2002. Dischord and Bug Records co-released it as Dischord No. 132.5.
years.xp: The half catalog number marks it as a Dischord co-release rather than a full label release.

years.cap: Justin Moyer at a show in Goleta, California, 2005
years.h: Antelope join Q and Not U and Black Eyes on tour
years.p: Dischord's band history calls it an extensive tour of the United States in September 2003. Two DC bands were pushing punk toward dance music and chaos; Antelope pushed it toward space.
years.xp: Dischord's history says Antelope first played regional shows in eastern and midwestern US cities before that tour. By 2007 the band was also playing dates with Joe Lally and Soccer Team, according to the same history.

years.h: Crowns/The Flock goes to Inner Ear with MacKaye producing
years.p: The two-song single is Dischord No. 142. [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produced it at Inner Ear Studios. It came out on 7-inch, now out of print, and on CD.

eras.title: One album in the Dischord House, then done
eras.text: A full-length took until 2007, and it was made in the house where the label lives. Elvy, Andre and Moyer broke up the following year.

years.h: Reflector, made in the Dischord House
years.p: Antelope and [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produced the band's only full-length at the Dischord House in Arlington in late 2006. It came out in 2007 as Dischord No. 157.
years.xp:
Ten songs, from the title track to "Collective Dream," including "Justin Jesus." TJ Lipple mastered it. PopMatters gave it 7 out of 10, called it "unclassifiable," and heard Prince and Delta 5, staccato grooves and ping-ponging guitar and bass riffs stitched together with short bits of silence.

The same review got the facts wrong, calling Antelope a Justin Moyer solo project. Dischord's credits list three players, with Elvy and Andre both on drums, bass and vocals.

years.h: Live at the First Unitarian Church, Philadelphia, September 11, 2006
yt: Live at the First Unitarian Church, Philadelphia, September 11, 2006

years.h: The last show is 19 April 2008 at Circle of Hope, Philadelphia
years.p: Dischord's history gives the breakup one line. Three releases, one of them a full-length, and then the band was finished.

eras.title: Moyer and Andre, still at it
eras.text: The partnership outlived the band. Moyer kept making records under several names while writing for the Washington Post, and Andre turned up next to him again.

years.p: [[Justin Moyer|68cb15fd-5c0c-4b60-ad06-935ac0756a4d]] and [[Mike Andre|18f336ed-8cdb-4b22-9186-daedae20bf66]] start Puff Pieces with Amanda Huron. The self-titled album lands in 2014, Bland in D.C. in 2016.
